description:
Van Hollen vs Schumer: does Chuck Schumer have the votes to stay Senate Democratic leader? We counted all 55 Democratic senators from what each has said on the record before the Dec. 1 secret ballot.

Chris Van Hollen told Jen Psaki on MS NOW that he has "more than ten"; minutes later Schumer posted that he has the votes. By our count 18 senators are in Schumer's column, 9 are against him and 28 have said neither. Inside: who those 28 are (the newcomers, committee chairs like Patty Murray and Jack Reed, and the left), why a secret ballot changes the math (in 1971 Ted Kennedy counted 28 promises and got 24 votes), each man's pitch (the Dec. 11 funding fight, the primaries, the money behind the wins, a quieter leader), Chris Pappas's one ballot, and what 45, the mid-thirties or 33 votes would mean for Schumer.
